children: Shares of Advanced Micro Devices
have rallied 35% over the last 30 days, hitting a new 52-week high of $639 per share on Sept. 25.
We asked Seeking Alpha analysts
and
if they think the stock still has upside following its most recent rally.
I don't think AMD
still has upside after its latest rally. The firm has an incredibly lofty valuation to grow into, well above peers like Nvidia
Furthermore, its largest customer, Meta
, whose deal involved substantial equity, is now working with Broadcom
to build custom silicon, the same custom silicon peers like Google
and Amazon
have scaled into the gigawatts.
We think it's a matter of time before Meta
does the same, which will compress AMD's margins and stop its ability to grow into its valuation.
(The Value Portfolio leads SA investing group The Retirement Forum.)
Fundamental Options: In a base-case scenario, where I tried to be a bit on the conservative side, the DCF fair value that I estimated for AMD

a few days ago was $553. In a pessimistic scenario, with reduced TAM for GPUs and server CPUs and lower perpetual growth, the fair value would be around $395. In an optimistic scenario, with a higher perpetual growth rate and a lower discount rate, the fair value would be $733; if we add higher TAM and market share, then $800+.

While I can't assign exact probabilities to the three scenarios, the chances are more or less evenly distributed, but likely with a slight edge for the optimistic scenario, as I tried to be a bit conservative in my base case. Significant upside potential exists only in the optimistic scenario. In the base case scenario, once the fair value reaches the current price in approximately one year, an annual growth of ~10.5% (the discount rate) would follow.

I gradually trimmed part of my position following sharp gains to protect myself against the pessimistic scenario. I’m holding a portion to benefit from the optimistic scenario. I hedged the remaining portion for the base-case scenario.
